native-linux/rescan-with-baseline.note: same tree, --baseline-index and --expected-files given: the walk's cost and 0 baseline passes (was 1 full decompress and parse, only to read the root's file count)

native-linux/walk.note: 4 dirs, 4 files (one a second hardlink), 2 symlinks: 1 listing per dir, 1 fstatat per entry, symlinks included (jwalk took 8: no stat for symlinks)

native-macos/rescan-with-baseline.note: same tree, --baseline-index and --expected-files given: the walk's cost and 0 baseline passes (was 1 full decompress and parse, only to read the root's file count)

native-macos/walk.note: 4 dirs, 4 files (one a second hardlink), 2 symlinks: 1 listing per dir, 1 lstat per dir (its index mtime); getattrlistbulk gives files and symlinks theirs. jwalk took 8 stats: it also lstat'ed every file

native-windows/parallel.note: 4 dirs (2 under the root), 4 files: the parallel walker runs; 1 listing per dir, 1 stat (root mtime)

native-windows/root-with-one-subfolder.note: 3 dirs in a chain, 1 file each: 1 listing per dir, 1 stat (root mtime; subfolders take theirs from the parent listing). Was 4 listings, root files twice

native-windows/root-without-subfolders.note: root with 3 files and no subfolders: 1 listing, 1 stat (root mtime). Was 2 listings, with every root file counted and indexed twice

native-windows/unchanged-root.note: rescan of the parallel tree with nothing changed: 1 stat (root mtime, handed to the sequential walker, which used to stat it again), no listings, 2 baseline passes (load, then copy the inherited files)
